newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Opposition walks out of besieged Sofia parliament.
newsitem.headline: Opposition walks out of besieged Sofia parliament.

text.p: Opposition deputies walked out of Bulgaria's besieged parliament on Friday, saying they wanted to protect anti-government demonstrators outside the building.

"We are leaving this parliament and we are walking out physically because the risk for you outside the parliament is greater than for those inside," said the leader of the main opposition Union of Democratic Forces (UDF), Ivan Kostov.
"We are here as a guarantee for your safety," Kostov said outside the building, which was surrounded by double cordons of riot police.
Deputies of the ruling Socialist party, protected by interior ministry troops, remain stranded in parliament, fearing the crowds will attack them if they try to leave.
President Zhelyu Zhelev, who returned from France on Friday, was expected to visit parliament later in the evening.

The UDF deputies walked out after the ex-communist ruling party refused to vote on an opposition declaration calling for early elections and proposed combining it with elements of their motion proposing dialogue.
"We will start preparations for a nationwide political strike and we believe everyone will join us," Kostov said.
"After this clash and this lack of understanding, we believe there is no possibility for us to stay and keep on working in this parliament."
Dozens of demonstrators forced their way into the building earlier in the day. Police fought them back, spraying them with tear gas and water and barricading the corridors with tables and chairs.
